name: Cyclosporine A versus pentosan polysulfate
question: Does oral cyclosporine A improve urinary frequency and symptoms more than pentosan polysulfate sodium in interstitial cystitis?

arms.label: pentosan polysulfate sodium 100 mg three times daily

design.population: Sixty-four patients with interstitial cystitis meeting National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases criteria (53 women and 11 men); 15 had Hunner's ulcers (5 cyclosporine, 10 PPS).
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 2235–2236; Results, p 2236

verdictNote: Halved daily frequency in 11/32 versus 0/32; adverse events occurred in 30/32 versus 18/32.
takeaway: In 64 patients with interstitial cystitis, six months of cyclosporine A halved daily micturition frequency in 11/32 patients versus 0/32 with pentosan polysulfate sodium (P below 0.001). Global response was 24/32 versus 6/32; adverse events occurred in 30/32 versus 18/32.

reports.label: Primary comparative report
reports.citation: Sairanen J, Tammela TL, Leppilahti M, et al. "Cyclosporine A and pentosan polysulfate sodium for the treatment of interstitial cystitis: a randomized comparative study." *J Urol.* 2005;174(6):2235-2238. doi:10.1097/01.ju.0000181808.45786.84
reports.followUpLocator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 2235

results.endpoint: At least 50% reduction in daily micturition frequency
results.measure: Patients whose 24-hour micturition frequency was halved at six months; randomized-arm denominators
results.note: Absolute percentage-point difference calculated from counts. The paper gives no confidence interval or explicit ITT label; its prespecified two-sided significance threshold was P <0.05.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods and Results, p 2236

results.measure: Mean change in micturitions per 24 hours at six months; difference in mean changes
results.note: Difference in mean changes calculated from arm values; Table 2 gives no analysis-set denominator or confidence interval. Twenty-nine patients per arm completed six months.

results.measure: Subjective global response assessment at six months; percentage-point difference
results.note: GRA categories 4–6 counted as response; absolute percentage-point difference calculated from counts.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 2236; Table 3, p 2237

results.measure: Mean change in nightly episodes after six months
results.note: Difference calculated from arm-specific mean changes; no confidence interval reported.

results.measure: Mean change on 0–10 cm VAS after six months
results.note: Difference calculated from arm-specific mean changes; no confidence interval reported.

harms.label: Adverse events
harms.locator: Full text, Results, p 2236; Table 5, p 2237
harms.note: Table 5 reports each participant's worst adverse-event severity (grades 0–3), not Clavien-Dindo grades.

harms.label: Blood pressure and renal toxicity

values.exp: 2/32 had clinically significant diastolic blood-pressure increases; 1/32 had creatinine rise despite dose reduction

harms.note: Cyclosporine dose was halved for the two blood-pressure events; the creatinine rise normalized after drug discontinuation.

delivery.label: Oral treatment regimen

values.exp: Cyclosporine A 1.5 mg/kg twice daily for six months
values.ctl: Pentosan polysulfate sodium 100 mg three times daily for six months

delivery.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, pp 2235–2236
delivery.note: Blood pressure and serum creatinine were checked monthly in the cyclosporine arm.

delivery.label: Cyclosporine dose reduction or discontinuation for intolerance

values.exp: 4/32 required a 50% dose reduction; 3/32 discontinued within one month

delivery.locator: Full text, Results, pp 2236–2237; Discussion, p 2238
delivery.note: Seven of 32 cyclosporine recipients did not tolerate the starting dose.

reports.label: Quality-of-life analysis
reports.citation: Sairanen J, Leppilahti M, Tammela TL, et al. "Evaluation of health-related quality of life in patients with painful bladder syndrome/interstitial cystitis and the impact of four treatments on it." *Scand J Urol Nephrol.* 2009;43(3):212-219. doi:10.1080/00365590802671031
reports.followUp: Quality of life before and after six months of oral treatment

results.measure: Emotional well-being, social functioning, activity limitation days, pain, and physical capacity after oral treatment
results.note: Cyclosporine had a greater effect than PPS across the listed domains; the abstract gives no arm-specific scores. This report also analyzed a separate DMSO-versus-BCG trial.
